content.value_statement: Influencer campaign budgets are difficult to balance across creators, platforms, and content formats. This skill builds allocations, projections, scenarios, and reallocation recommendations from your inputs.
actual_capabilities: Allocates spend across influencer tiers, platforms, content formats, amplification, tools, gifting, and contingency.
Applies built-in Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube cost benchmarks with industry multipliers.
Projects reach, impressions, engagements, EMV, CPM, CPE, CPC, ROI, and ROAS when inputs support them.
Compares conservative, recommended, and aggressive budget scenarios with a stated recommendation.
Identifies concentration, contingency, cost-efficiency, and creator-selection budget risks.
Recommends mid-campaign reallocations when spend and creator performance data are provided.
limitations: Built-in costs and performance projections are estimates until replaced with current rate cards or measured data.
The skill does not create the full campaign strategy or recruit influencers.
It does not read live ad pacing, change bids, or execute budget changes.
Optional connector data depends on connector availability and the quality of source records.

use_cases.title: Plan a Product Launch
use_cases.description: Build a platform and creator-tier allocation with projected reach, engagement, and contingency.

use_cases.title: Compare Client Budget Options
use_cases.description: Present three spend scenarios with costs, expected outcomes, tradeoffs, and a recommended option.

use_cases.title: Reallocate Active Campaign Spend
use_cases.description: Compare planned and actual results, then move remaining funds toward stronger creators or channels.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Allocation
prompt_templates.prompt: Allocate [budget] across [platforms] for a [campaign goal] influencer campaign. Include creator tiers, content, amplification, and contingency.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting with a total budget and basic campaign goal.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Budget Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [low], [target], and [high] budgets for [audience] on [platforms]. Recommend one scenario and explain the tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when stakeholders need several funding options.

prompt_templates.title: Project Campaign Returns
prompt_templates.prompt: Optimize [budget] using these rates and performance assumptions: [data]. Project CPM, CPE, conversions, ROI, and ROAS. Label every metric source.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when rate cards or measured campaign data are available.

prompt_templates.title: Reallocate Mid-Campaign Spend
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned allocation, spend to date, and creator performance: [data]. Reallocate the remaining budget while preserving [constraints]. Quantify expected impact.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an active campaign has enough performance data for optimization.

output_examples.input: Allocate $30,000 across TikTok and Instagram for a Gen Z skincare launch.
output: TikTok creators: $15,000 across micro and nano tiers.
Instagram creators: $9,000 for Reels, posts, and Stories.
Projected reach, engagement, CPM, and ROI are labeled Estimated.

output_examples.output: The recommended $75,000 scenario balances macro reach with micro creator volume, preserves contingency, and avoids excessive concentration.

output_examples.input: Reallocate $12,000 remaining after reviewing creator performance.
output_examples.output: Move $7,000 from underperforming placements to the strongest creators, reserve $3,000 for amplification, and retain $2,000 as contingency.

best_practices: Provide current rate cards, target platforms, audience, timeline, goal, and fixed costs before requesting an allocation.
Label all numbers as Measured, User-provided, or Estimated, and document every major assumption.
Keep five to ten percent as contingency and review performance before reallocating active spend.
anti_patterns: Do not treat benchmark ranges as guaranteed creator prices or campaign results.
Do not place more than forty percent of the budget with one creator without documenting concentration risk.
Do not execute reallocations from projections alone when current performance data is available.

faq.question: Which platforms does the skill cover?
faq.answer: It includes built-in benchmarks for Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube. User-provided data can support other platforms.

faq.question: Does it need live integrations?
faq.answer: No. It works from provided inputs and built-in benchmarks. Optional connectors can replace estimates with current rates and measured results.

faq.question: Can it calculate ROI and ROAS?
faq.answer: Yes, when the required value, conversion, and revenue assumptions are available. Otherwise, it reports clearly labeled estimates.

faq.question: Can it optimize paid advertising budgets?
faq.answer: It can plan channel allocation and ROAS scenarios. It does not read live pacing, choose bid strategies, or execute changes.

faq.question: Can it reallocate an active campaign?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide spend to date and creator-level results so it can compare performance and recommend remaining-budget moves.

faq.question: Does it replace campaign planning?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on allocation, projections, scenarios, and reallocation. Campaign strategy and creator recruitment remain separate tasks.
